description: Build ANY number of 3D solids from one node — add a row per kind (Cuboid, Cylinder, Sphere, Cone, Capsule, Frustum, Tapered Box, Torus, Polyhedron, Tube, Ring, Loft), each with its own dimensions, position, colour and input endpoint. The 3D twin of the 2D Render node, and the single entry point for 3D geometry.
instructions:
One node for the whole 3D output of an operation. Press "Add primitive" for a row, pick its KIND, set its dimensions, and — optionally — wire a POSITION LIST into that row's own `valin-<rowId>` endpoint on the left.

A ROW IS A STYLE GROUP, NOT A SOLID. With nothing wired, a row builds ONE solid at its own X / Y / Z. Wire it a list and it builds one solid PER POINT, all sharing the row's dimensions and colour:
• `[[x,y],…]` — one solid per point, at the row's Z.
• `[[x,y,z],…]` — a third column gives each solid its own base elevation.
So a Math Engine that computes twelve column positions needs ONE row, not twelve Cuboid nodes.

KINDS
• CUBOID — Length × Breadth × Height.
• CYLINDER — Radius + Height.
• SPHERE — Radius, resting on the floor at Y=0.
• CONE — Radius + Height, base on the floor.
• CAPSULE — a pill: Radius caps on a straight middle of Length, so it stands Length + 2 × Radius tall.
• FRUSTUM — a tapered cylinder: Radius at the bottom → Top radius over Height. Equal radii give a cylinder, a top of 0 gives a cone.
• TAPERED BOX — a rectangular frustum: Length × Breadth at the bottom → Top length × Top breadth over Height.
• TORUS — a donut lying FLAT: Radius is the ring (hole centre → tube centre), Tube radius the section, Arc° the sweep (360 closes it, less leaves an open arc — a partial ring with no boolean). Positioned by a point; use RING instead when the axis is computed.
• POLYHEDRON — no dimensions at all: the wired FACE LIST is the entire solid, exactly as the 2D Polygon row's vertex list is the entire outline. This is the kind to use when the SHAPE itself is computed, because a Cuboid row's Length / Breadth / Height are fixed numbers that no wire can reach — a Math Engine that derives a solid from its parameters emits it here and the mesh stays parametric.
• TUBE — a capped cylinder along a wired AXIS SEGMENT, one per row of the list. Radius comes from the row; a SEVENTH column gives a segment its own radius.
• RING — a torus whose AXIS is the wired segment: centred on the segment's MIDPOINT and lying in the plane perpendicular to it. Only the segment's direction and midpoint are read — its length is free — so a wheel is driven by its axle. Radius is the ring (hole centre → tube centre) and Tube radius the section; a SEVENTH column overrides the ring radius per segment and an EIGHTH the section.
• LOFT — the SKIN over a stack of cross-sections. It reads the same grouped point list a Polyhedron row does, but a run of equal group value is a SECTION, not a finished face: consecutive sections are stitched quad by quad and both ends are capped. This is the row for a curved BODY — a car, a boat hull, a roof, a moulding, a tapered column. Polyhedron can draw any of those, but only if the Math Engine enumerates every face, which means hand-writing the same stitching loop (k → k+1 around the ring, i → i+1 along the body, the wrap-around, the two caps) in every flow that lofts anything. What actually varies between one lofted thing and the next is the SECTIONS, so that is all a flow authors. Sections should share a vertex count; where two differ they are stitched over the smaller, so a mismatch loses detail rather than the solid. Rings close automatically — do not repeat the first point. Fewer than two usable sections draws nothing.

THE TUBE / RING WIRE FORMAT — an AXIS-SEGMENT list `[[x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2],…]`, one segment per solid, in the same plan-frame metres everything else uses. These two are the only rows that carry their own ORIENTATION: a Cuboid / Cylinder row is positioned by a POINT and its axis is fixed vertical, and the row exposes no rotation for a wire to reach, so every off-axis member — a raked fork, a diagonal strut, a handrail, a wheel standing on edge — was previously unbuildable except by hand-authoring its faces into a Polyhedron row. A tilted segment needs no special case: the perpendicular frame is derived from the segment itself, so a vertical seat tube and a raked fork take the same path. Internally each row is emitted as a face list on the Polyhedron path, so the viewport, the 3D export and any downstream Display 3D treat it identically. A degenerate (zero-length) segment is skipped, and a row with nothing parseable wired draws nothing.

THE POLYHEDRON WIRE FORMAT — a list of FACES, each an ordered ring of 3D points (metres, plan frame). Two shapes, mirroring the Polygon row one-for-one:
• NESTED `[[[x,y,z],…],…]` — one inner array per face.
• FLAT `[[x,y,z,f],…]` — one face per run of equal FOURTH value, the group column a Math Engine writes with `hcat(ring, fill(rows(ring),1,f))`. A 3-column flat list with no group column is a single face.
Rings may have any vertex count and differ face to face; each is fan-triangulated and drawn double-sided, so winding direction doesn't matter. A ring of fewer than 3 points is dropped, and a row with nothing parseable wired draws nothing (unlike Cuboid / Cylinder, it has no fallback shape of its own).
A closed box is 6 rings of 4 points; a whole assembly is just more rings in the same list, so ONE row can carry a nine-part piece of furniture — see Workflows/Miscellaneous/bed-flow.json, which builds all nine boxes in a Math Engine loop.
X / Y / Z on a Polyhedron row are an OFFSET applied to the finished mesh (its vertices are already absolute), not a position the shape is built at.

COORDINATES are metres in the same plan frame the 2D side uses (X across, Y down the plan, Z up), matching a wired `val-points` list exactly, so the solids land over the geometry that generated them.

COLOUR is per row. LAYER is kept on the row as a label only — the 3D scene has no canvas layers; its styling is this colour plus any downstream Display 3D node.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT REPLACE: the single-purpose 3D primitives (Cuboid, Cylinder, Sphere, Cone, Frustum …) with their transform / boolean / display chain. Those stay the way to hand-model one solid with full control. This node is for solids that arrive computed — one row, many instances.
